title: The Hot Chocolate Trap
notes: Recurring detective-cast convention: Conan Edogawa omitted (he performs the deduction, voiced through Sonoko via the usual bowtie-voice-changer device, but never a suspect). Kogoro Mouri and Inspector Megure do not appear this episode -- the investigating officer is a different, episode-local character, Inspector Yuminaga, who is included as a person node since he drives a significant chunk of on-screen investigation (initially closes the case as a static-electricity accident, then is corrected). Ran and Sonoko ARE kept per the old case file's note that this episode treats them as present, questioned participants rather than incidental cast. Discrepancy vs. the old lower-fidelity file: that file listed Ran (s2) and Sonoko (s3) with roles/edges implying they were genuine suspects ("knows" edges to the victim, was_at with the culprit). The transcript never develops any accusation, motive, or real suspicion against either of them -- they are present witnesses only, formally cleared by simply not being implicated by any evidence. This rebuild drops the unsupported suspect framing for them rather than inventing motive edges to match the old file. The old file also modeled the case with generic `event` nodes (e1-e3) and a single generic `knows` edge type; this rebuild replaces those with direct typed verb edges per schema v3, and reserves `clue` nodes for the three genuinely comparative facts (photo vs. physical state of the pot; Ran's corrected memory of the flame sequence; Sakura's sleeve-burn location vs. her claimed distance from the victim). Per the 2026-08 batch-8+ scoping change, temporal fields (order/temporal_frame/years_before_present) are omitted from all edges. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Photo shows Tsujimoto drinking plain water from the pot right before the show, yet the pot held salt water during the show -- only Sakura handled it afterward, so only she could have salted it.

Ran's corrected memory: a huge flame flared up BEFORE the bottles fell, contradicting the assumed order (bottles fall, liquor catches) -- proves an ignition device fired first, not an accidental spark.

Sakura claimed she was far from Tsujimoto when the fire spread, but her burned sleeve matches alcohol splashing on her while she rigged the hidden spirytus container under the table -- contradicts her claimed distance.
